data.description:
Spine task 2 of D1 v1. Create apps/invoicing/ — the product application — in the stack chosen by the stack-decision task: docker compose service(s), configuration loading, a test harness, and a health endpoint. The acceptance property that matters: docker compose up starts the app and the full test suite passes with NO external services, NO accounts, and NO network egress. Everything after this depends on that property continuing to hold.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 row C-02 (IN — Rule 1: nothing in the chain runs without it). Section 8.3 spine task 2.

DECISION CONTEXT. The directory name apps/invoicing/ is decided, not a placeholder. Under the company-name record docs/strategy/09-company-name.md section 8.2, the monorepo/internal-infra layer carries generic descriptive names and the product brand attaches at the extraction seam and on customer-facing surfaces (deploy domains, sender domains, app chrome). The product has no name yet and this directory never needs to change when it gets one — which is also why naming does not block the scaffold. Follow apps/chat/ for compose and test-runner conventions unless the stack decision chose otherwise; note that the chat app is internal tooling and its zero-dependency convention is evidence, not a mandate, for the product.

VERIFICATION: docker compose up serves the health endpoint; the test suite runs green from a clean checkout with the network unavailable. Both are runnable today with no accounts.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the data model or any table (the data-model task); any Stripe code whatsoever — the custody guard lands before any Stripe caller and this task must not front-run it with a "temporary" client; authentication; any UI screen (screens are wireframe-gated on AS-30).
data.title: D1 v1: apps/invoicing scaffold — compose stack, config, test harness, health check

data.note: spine: scaffold cannot start before the stack is chosen

data.body:
PLAN FILED. Branch feat/AS-37-invoicing-scaffold, worktree .worktrees/AS-37. Marcus implements from the plan file alone; everything binding is quoted or cited there.

THE TWO GAPS AS-36's REVIEW LEFT ME, both closed by measurement rather than assertion.

(1) PINS. The decision mandates exact pins and never names them. Named now, measured 2026-09-01: express@5.2.1 (MIT), ejs@6.0.1 (Apache-2.0), base image node:24.20.0-slim (exact patch, stronger than the mandated exact minor). Plus the rule that regenerates them if npm has moved: pin the latest stable at implementation time as an exact literal, re-walk the tree, and STOP for a board ask if any licence is non-permissive or the direct set is anything but {express, ejs}.

ADOPTED TRANSITIVE FOOTPRINT, stated for the first time (QA finding 3): 2 direct, 67 distinct name@version, 69 instances, 4.0 MB, image 239 MB (+9 MB over base). Licence spread 61 MIT / 4 ISC / 1 Apache-2.0 / 1 BSD-3-Clause, zero non-permissive. Flagged in the plan: 67 is coincidentally the same number the decision reports for C2-WITH-Zod. It is arithmetic (Zod out, version drift in), not transcription — instances moved 70->69 and disk 12 MB->4.0 MB, consistent with 10.3.

A TRAP the decision does not warn about: 'npm install express@5.2.1' writes '^5.2.1' — a caret range, which section 12 explicitly forbids. Measured. Fix is --save-exact plus a committed lockfile plus npm ci only, and section 9.6 of the plan makes it a test rather than a review convention.

(2) TOKENS.CSS. Mechanism: repo-root build context (context ../.., dockerfile apps/invoicing/Dockerfile) with COPY docs/design/tokens/tokens.css ./vendor/tokens.css, served by an explicit named route registered before express.static. 'No copy' read as: exactly one copy in version control, and what is served is byte-identical to it — the only reading consistent with section 12's own Content-Length verification.

SPIKED, NOT REASONED. Built under BuildKit AND the legacy builder (chat's compose documents that this host sometimes exports DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0, which is why additional_contexts was rejected — BuildKit-only). Suite exit 0 under --network none. Served: 200, Content-Length 12199, body 12,199 bytes, byte-identical to the image source. MUTATION: delete the COPY line, rebuild — suite exits 1. The guard is not vacuous. Bind mount rejected because it puts the file out of reach of the mountless test service, so byte-identity could only ever be asserted lexically, never fetched.

VACUITY FLOOR (eight prior vacuous passes: AS-17, AS-26, four in AS-29 cycle 1, one in AS-29 hardening, one in AS-31's checker). Three structural properties from day one. V1: harness.test.js fails under ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1, so one command in both directions proves the test service runs the suite, a failure produces a non-zero exit, and compose surfaces it — a runner never observed to go red is not evidence, same argument the decision made for validating --network none with both controls. V2: cardinality before quantification — every assertion quantified over a discovered set is preceded by an exact-count assertion against a committed literal (183 token declarations, the suite's own file count, the direct dependency set). V3: the container is the subject — deployed-shape properties are asserted from inside the mountless test service against the real image.

HEALTH CHECK. Design rule: a health check may only assert things that can be FALSE while the process is still able to answer. Three checks as data (config, vendor_assets, views), 200 only if all pass, 503 with the failing check named. Each must be demonstrated able to fail or it is decoration. Stripe and the DB are deliberately absent — AS-39 appends a row, which is why the checks are a list.

PORT 8348. Measured free; 8347 is asc-chat-server-1 and is not to be disturbed; 3001/4000/4100/5432/7700/8799 are held by unrelated containers.

DIVERGENCES FROM apps/chat, argued not inherited: routes/ + a thin composition root (the decision's load-bearing finding is that hand-rolled code leaves module boundaries to discipline, and this company has two measured observations of that discipline not holding); express.static + an enumeration test instead of chat's STATIC_FILES allowlist (AS-17 was a missing allowlist entry — express.static has no second edit to forget, and the enumeration test closes its own failure direction); config injected into app.js so no test mutates process.env. Mirrored: compose-only, mountless test service, bare node --test, bind 0.0.0.0 inside with loopback on the host side, manifests COPY'd as data for a deploy-shape test.

PLATFORM PIN: kept at linux/amd64. My prior was that emulation would tax every suite run since we install 67 packages where chat installs none. Measured 3x3: native 1.63/1.59/1.56 s, emulated 1.58/1.47/1.49 s — no measurable tax, the suite is startup-dominated. Prior falsified, pin stands.

ONE HARNESS RULE that cost me a probe: register teardown BEFORE the assertions (t.after), never after. A probe that closed its listener on the line after a failing assert HUNG with no output until killed. A hung suite is worse than a red one — no exit code, no output.

MUST NOT FORECLOSE (AS-38's guard is not this task's job, but a scaffold can quietly make it unenforceable): no outbound HTTP client anywhere outside test/ — the decision chose the hand-rolled client precisely because the only bypass is a second HTTP client and fetch/node:http call sites are greppable; no stripe dep, no STRIPE_* key, no /webhook, no application_fee; no money type (AS-39 owns integer minor units + currency); network_mode: none is not negotiable (T3); dependency budget stays at 2, enforced by a test.

NO ACCOUNT ASSUMED. AS-51 is open and stays off the critical path: no setting is required, no credential is named, no .env of any kind, and the acceptance property is that the suite passes with a COMPLETELY EMPTY environment. The optional-secret mechanism and redaction are built and tested now against a fixture schema, so AS-38 inherits a tested mechanism rather than an untested one.

WRITE-BACKS OWED to docs/engineering/01-stack-decision.md section 13, to be filed as a backlog task (not AS-37's — it must not amend the decision it implements): the pins and adopted footprint; T4 gains an upgrade clause re-running the transitive licence scan (QA finding 2, ACCEPTED — nothing today re-scans the 67 admitted packages when Express or EJS is upgraded, and section 5.3 is the proof that a tree is where a licence problem hides); and the caret-range trap.

ZERO SPEND. Two MIT/Apache-2.0 packages, no account, no service, no purchase.

AS-37 implementation complete on feat/AS-37-invoicing-scaffold (4 commits: d97ec82, 4b6fc45, 0e57bc0, fae6755). Suite: 66 tests, 66 pass, exit 0, mountless and network-blocked. Not transitioned, not merged, not pushed.

== THE FOUR GUARD DEMONSTRATIONS (real output, not assertions) ==

V1 — the runner is proven able to fail. Both directions on the final image:
  docker compose run --rm test                        -> EXIT=0   (tests 66, pass 66, fail 0)
  docker compose run --rm -e ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 test -> EXIT=1 (tests 66, pass 65, fail 1)
  The one failure is harness.test.js "V1: the runner can fail". Green means something.

V2 — cardinality before quantification. Demonstrated TWICE, each mutate/observe/restore atomic:
  (a) A test file silently leaves the suite: mv health.test.js health.test.js.disabled, rebuild, run
      -> EXIT=1, tests 54 (not 66), and "V2: the suite is exactly the files it is supposed to be" fired.
  (b) THE IMPORTANT ONE — the source scan mutated to examine zero files (extension filter -> /\.(nope)$/):
      -> EXIT=1, but only ONE test failed:
         FAIL: "the source scan examines exactly the files it is supposed to"
               AssertionError: expected 11 app source files, found 0:
         PASS: "no app source outside test/ contains an outbound HTTP client"
         PASS: "nothing AS-38 or AS-39 owns has leaked into the scaffold"
         PASS: "no file in apps/invoicing exceeds 1,200 lines"
      Three forbidden-construct assertions went GREEN on the empty set. Without the cardinality
      assertion the suite would have passed while scanning nothing — the AS-31 failure exactly.
      This is the ninth vacuous pass in this codebase and the first caught by a guard built in
      advance rather than by a reviewer afterward. Before anyone trims V2 as ceremony: it is the
      only thing that caught this, and it caught it on its first outing.

V3 — the container is the subject. Commented out COPY docs/design/tokens/tokens.css, rebuilt, ran:
  -> EXIT=1, tests 66, pass 55, fail 11. Caught by three independent mechanisms, not one:
     HTTP serving (4 tests in assets.test.js), manifest-as-data (3 in deploy-shape.test.js),
     and the health check (4 in health.test.js).
  Restored in the SAME step, rebuilt: EXIT=0, 66/66. Dockerfile verified byte-identical to HEAD.

HEALTH CHECKS — each demonstrated able to fail independently, live HTTP from the real image:
  BASELINE                              HTTP 200 ok=true    config pass / vendor_assets pass / views pass
  vendorDir -> /nonexistent             HTTP 503 ok=false   FAIL vendor_assets <- ENOENT; other two pass
  viewsDir  -> /nonexistent             HTTP 503 ok=false   FAIL views <- ENOENT; other two pass
  settings that never passed loadConfig HTTP 503 ok=false   FAIL config <- logLevel (INVOICING_LOG_LEVEL)
                                                            is not one of debug, info, warn, error
  Plus two more failure paths in the suite: a zero-byte tokens.css, and a template that exists but
  cannot render (views/ present, EJS broken) — the half a stat() would miss.

== THREE BUGS I CAUGHT IN MY OWN CHECKS ==
1. Substring match: a scan for forbidden packages "got"/"request" matched negotiator and
   body-parser's tree. Fixed to exact package-name matching, and the test now ASSERTS negotiator
   is present so the trap stays live and nobody "fixes" a future failure by loosening the matcher.
2. Prose counted as code: deploy-shape scanned the raw Dockerfile for "npm install" and hit its own
   comment "NEVER npm install"; the app source scan walked vendor/tokens.css, which exists only
   inside the image. Comments are stripped once (the stripper is itself tested, in both directions),
   vendor/ is excluded, and the test asserts the raw file DOES contain the phrase it must not trip on.
3. The empty-set pass in V2(b) above.
All three are the same family: a check that runs and measures the wrong thing.

== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ==
1  compose up --build -> web healthy; GET /healthz -> HTTP 200 {"ok":true}, all three checks pass. PASS
2  compose run --rm test -> EXIT=0; test service has network_mode: none and NO volumes. PASS
3  No .env* in apps/invoicing (find -> 0); suite passes with a completely empty environment. PASS
4  curl -sI /tokens.css -> Content-Length: 12199; diff against docs/design/tokens/tokens.css EMPTY. PASS
5  git ls-files | grep -c 'tokens\.css$' -> 1 (only docs/design/tokens/tokens.css). PASS
6  {"ejs":"6.0.1","express":"5.2.1"} — 2 direct deps, both exact literals; lockfile tracked;
   Dockerfile uses `npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund`; zero `npm install` instructions. PASS
7  Footprint recorded below. PASS
8  V1 both directions. PASS   9 Health checks fail. PASS   10 Tokens mutation red. PASS
11 Repo-root .dockerignore: .git, .worktrees, **/node_modules, apps/chat/data, .claude — asserted
   by deploy-shape.test.js. PASS
12 Largest file 303 lines (deploy-shape.test.js), limit 1,200. PASS
13 Zero hits across 11 app source files for: stripe import, STRIPE_, application_fee, /webhook,
   node:sqlite, axios, undici, fetch(, http.request( — all outside test/. PASS
14 asc-chat-server-1 on 8347: "Up 18 hours (healthy)" before AND after. Untouched. PASS
15 apps/invoicing/README.md: the two commands, the port, the tokens mechanism, AS-45's obligation. PASS

PINS (§4.3 rule applied, no delta from §4.1, so no re-measure was triggered):
  node:24-slim -> v24.20.0, pinned as node:24.20.0-slim (exact patch)
  express 5.2.1 MIT · ejs 6.0.1 Apache-2.0
  Direct 2 · distinct name@version 67 · instances 69 · 4.0 MB
  Licences: 61 MIT, 4 ISC, 1 Apache-2.0, 1 BSD-3-Clause · 0 non-permissive
  (67 distinct is the arithmetic coincidence §4.2 predicted, not a stale copy.)

== CHAT DB NOT IN THE IMAGE ==
The live DB exists in the main checkout (chat.db 126,976 B + a 4,062,352 B WAL). Exhaustive scan of
the product image for *.db, *.db-wal, *.db-shm, *.sqlite*, */apps/chat*: NOTHING FOUND. The full
/app tree is 20 files, all this app's plus the one vendored tokens.css.
Precision worth recording: the Dockerfile uses selective COPYs and never `COPY . .`, so the DB could
not have been baked in even without .dockerignore. What the ignore file actually prevents is the DB
entering the 10 MB build context sent to the daemon. Plan §5.4 slightly overstates the mechanism;
the file is still correct and still required, and both properties are now verified.

== DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN ==
1. build.platforms ADDED to compose.yaml. MEASURED: on Docker 29.6.1 / compose v5.3.0, service-level
   `platform: linux/amd64` alone silently produced a linux/arm64 image. `build.platforms` makes the
   pin take, under BOTH DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 and =0. The plan's §6.1 sketch would have shipped a
   native-arch image against an amd64 pin. deploy-shape.test.js now asserts both keys.
2. .dockerignore is COPY'd into the image. §9.3 requires deploy-shape to assert its exclusions from
   inside the mountless test service, which cannot reach the host checkout; §5.3's Dockerfile sketch
   listed only compose.yaml and Dockerfile. Necessary consequence, not a design change.
3. public/scaffold.css instead of public/.gitkeep. express.static ignores dotfiles, so a .gitkeep-only
   public/ would make the AS-17 enumeration guard scan zero reachable files — which V2 forbids from
   reporting success. A real app-owned asset gives the guard something to guard; it also keeps the
   scaffold page's styles out of the template. Enumeration literal is 1.
4. routes/pages.js added for GET /. The plan's §3.1 layout lists only routes/health.js and
   routes/assets.js, but §7.5 requires the scaffold page and §3.3(a) puts routes in routes/<area>.js.
   Putting it in app.js would have contradicted the plan's own boundary rule.
5. lib/vendor.js and lib/views.js added as registries, so routes and the health check share one list
   and V2 has a committed literal to count against.
6. withServer(config, fn) uses try/finally rather than t.after — matches the plan's stated signature
   and satisfies §8.4's rule by construction: teardown cannot be skipped when an assertion throws.
7. The `views` health check RENDERS each template with sampleLocals rather than stat'ing the
   directory. Stronger, and demonstrated failing on a broken template.
Size: 23 files in apps/invoicing + 2 touched outside (plan projected ~21); §1.2's keep-it-whole
justification holds.

TECHNIQUE NOTE for QA, learned the hard way: a mutation test interrupted between mutate and restore
leaves the repo in the broken state it was demonstrating. Bind the restore to the command's EXIT trap
and treat mutate/observe/restore as one indivisible step. Also rebuild after restoring — I restored a
source tree but left the mutant IMAGE in place, and only an image-contents check caught it.

OWED, NOT DONE (§14): the write-back backlog task folding the pins, the adopted footprint, T4's
upgrade clause, and the npm-caret hazard into docs/engineering/01-stack-decision.md §13 is NOT yet
filed. The numbers are above. Left to the CTO/orchestrator since I was scoped to comment only.

QA review (Priya Raman), part 1 — recorded incrementally; session keeps getting interrupted. NOT A VERDICT YET.

SEQUENCE NOTE: I have NOT yet read Marcus's implementer comment. Plan section 13 step 7 requires me to independently re-walk the dependency tree and THEN compare it against the number he recorded; reading it earlier would anchor the measurement. I will read it at step 7 and say so in the verdict.

BASELINE (protocol step 2): docker compose run --rm --build test from apps/invoicing => 66 tests, 66 pass, 0 fail, exit 0, 1.37s. Start state: asc-chat-server-1 Up 19h healthy on 127.0.0.1:8347, untouched.

GUARD V1 — BROKEN BY ME, CONFIRMED REAL (protocol step 3).
  with -e ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 => exit 1, harness.test.js:33 fails as designed.
  without it                    => exit 0.
Run in both directions, so this is not a report I am accepting on trust: the test service really runs the suite, a failing assertion really produces a non-zero exit, and compose really surfaces that exit. Every subsequent green in this review is now interpretable.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (protocol step 1) — PASS. Zero .lattice/ paths on the branch; board state stayed on master. Files outside apps/invoicing are exactly .dockerignore and .gitignore, both authorised by plan section 3.1. Nothing else leaked.

CRITERION 5 — PASS. git ls-files | grep -c tokens.css => 1 (docs/design/tokens/tokens.css only).

CRITERION 3 (partial) — no .env file of any kind exists in apps/invoicing. Scrubbed-environment suite run still to come.

MUTATION HYGIENE — technique note for the house, not a finding. Implementation left a mutation live between mutate and restore. I am running every mutation as ONE indivisible bash call: cp to backup, then trap restore EXIT, then mutate, then observe; the trap fires; then git diff HEAD proves restoration before I move on. The trap makes restoration survive a failed command, a non-zero exit, and an interrupted shell. Recommend adopting this as the repo standard for mutation testing rather than leaving it a per-reviewer habit.

STILL TO DO: V3 tokens-COPY mutation; V2 cardinality guards including whether a zero-file scan can report success; each health sub-check driven red independently; container-vs-host; independent dependency re-walk then Marcus's comment; right-sizing verdict; section 11 forbidden-construct greps.

QA review (Priya Raman), part 2 — guards V3 and V2, broken by my own hand. Still not a verdict.

GUARD V3 (tokens COPY) — BROKEN BY ME, CONFIRMED REAL, AND STRONGER THAN LEXICAL.
Method: one indivisible bash call — cp Dockerfile to backup, trap restore EXIT, comment out the 'COPY docs/design/tokens/tokens.css ./vendor/tokens.css' line, rebuild, run, restore, then git diff HEAD to prove restoration.
Result: MUTANT_EXIT=1. 66 tests, 55 pass, 11 FAIL. Restored clean (git diff HEAD empty).
What matters is WHICH 11 failed, because it separates a real guard from a text scan of the Dockerfile:
  - RUNTIME layer, assets.test.js (4): GET /tokens.css byte-identical; the sentinel/183-declaration test; HEAD /tokens.css; the public/ shadow test. These fetch the real bytes out of the real image through the real serving path.
  - MANIFEST layer, deploy-shape.test.js (3): parser corpus counts; tokens COPY present; no second copy into vendor/.
  - HEALTH layer (1): GET /healthz 200-with-all-three-passing went red, i.e. vendor_assets detected the missing asset at runtime.
  - 3 further health tests failed because they assert EXCLUSIVITY (deepEqual(failing, ['views']) etc.) and vendor_assets was now also red. That is the exclusivity assertion working, not a defect.
So the guard is genuinely runtime-backed. Deleting the COPY cannot be hidden by editing a manifest assertion.

GUARD V2 (cardinality before quantification) — BROKEN BY ME, CONFIRMED REAL, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING HOLDING THREE OTHER GUARDS UP.
Method: same indivisible pattern on test/dependency-policy.test.js; changed the source-scan extension filter so appSourceFiles() matched nothing, making APP_SOURCES empty. Rebuild, run, restore, git diff HEAD clean.
Result: MUTANT_EXIT=1. 66 tests, 65 pass, 1 FAIL. The single failure was 'the source scan examines exactly the files it is supposed to' (the cardinality assertion, 11 files).
The three assertions that quantify over that set ALL PASSED GREEN ON THE EMPTY SET:
  PASS 'no app source outside test/ contains an outbound HTTP client'
  PASS 'nothing AS-38 or AS-39 owns has leaked into the scaffold'
  PASS 'no file in apps/invoicing exceeds 1,200 lines'
CONSEQUENCE, and this is why it matters beyond AS-37: those three assertions are the standing protection for AS-38's custody chokepoint, which does not exist yet. The stack decision chose a hand-rolled Stripe client specifically because the only bypass is a second HTTP client and those call sites stay greppable — the grep IS this scan. Without the cardinality assertion, a scan that silently stopped examining files would have reported success while protecting nothing, inertly, across the next thirteen tasks that build on this scaffold. This is the AS-31 failure mode exactly, and V2 is the only thing that catches it. It earns its place.

MUTATION TECHNIQUE — proposing this as the house standard, not my private habit. Every mutation above ran as ONE bash call: cp to backup; 'trap restore EXIT'; mutate; assert the mutation actually applied (guard against a silently-failed edit); observe; explicit restore; 'git diff HEAD' to prove restoration before moving on. This caught a real incident mid-review: one mutation's edit failed to apply, my post-mutation assertion aborted the run before I could observe a meaningless green, and the trap restored the file. Both properties are needed — the trap for interruption, the applied-check so a no-op mutation cannot be misread as 'the guard did not fire'.

REMAINING: health sub-checks driven red individually; container-vs-host; independent dependency re-walk then Marcus's comment; empty-env run; right-sizing verdict; verdict.
